rationale:
Neither design can be default-on. Under the adoption rule a design needs both the acceptance gates and a gain of at least 3 balanced points on BOTH externals. Each design passes one half and fails the other.

- F6-slot-rule-v2: acceptance passes everywhere (99.6% bench test, 98.5% LongMemEval, 98.4% LoCoMo). The balanced gain fails: +2.6 on LongMemEval and +0.0 on LoCoMo.
- F6-answerability-model: the gain passes as a point estimate (+5.9 LongMemEval, +6.2 LoCoMo). External acceptance fails badly: 78.5% and 76.1% against the 90% gate.

I re-derived every headline number from the verifiers' row-level outputs and they match.
- Slot rule: heldout/replay_heldout_all.json, and the verifier's official bench_test_v2/results.md (hybrid_full 99.6 / 17.4 / 58.5).
- Answerability model: verify-answerability-model/runs/v_*.json gives 240/247 + 12/23, 369/470 + 10/30, and 1172/1540 + 162/446.

Why the slot rule ships opt-in and the answerability model ships nothing this round:

1. The slot rule is safe as frozen. It is not worse than no-abstention on any held-out set, it adds no dependencies or downloads, it costs about 0.01 ms per ask, and the library default is off.
   - It also fixes a real bug in the snapshot. evaluation/systems.answer_extractive calls generation.answer(..., abstain_threshold=...), but the snapshot's answer() has no such parameter, so `--abstain-threshold` raises TypeError. The slot-rule patch adds the parameter. The answerability patch leaves the bug in place.
   - Its value is real only on benchmark-style "attribute never stated" questions (bench test p=0.0002). On the externals it is noise (LongMemEval p=0.096, LoCoMo precision 22.6% equals the 22.5% base rate). Hence experimental opt-in, not a headline feature.

2. The answerability model has the stronger signal: LoCoMo gain CI [+3.8, +8.7], bench test 74.7% balanced. But it has blocking defects that the frozen numbers do not cover.
   - (a) A failed model load is never cached. Every ask retries the network: 23 s per ask with the connection refused, 393 s per ask behind a dropping firewall. It also downloads 111 MB into data/rag/models during a request.
   - (b) The '<speaker>: ' passage prefix makes QNLI read any other person's passage as an answer, scoring about +5.8 against -7.3 without the prefix. The attribution filter fails open when the named person is not a speaker.
   - The verifier's fix for (b) is to change passage_text and re-tune. That invalidates the frozen held-out numbers, so the model would need a new dev-only tune, a new freeze and a single new held-out run before it can be merged even as opt-in.
   - Its external gains also rest on one component each. Without the paraphrase, LongMemEval drops to +2.8. Without speaker attribution, LoCoMo drops to +2.7, and that filter matches how LoCoMo category 5 is built and never fires on single-user stores.
   - The LongMemEval gain is not significant (CI [-2.7, +14.7]).
   - The designer's "evidence not retrieved" diagnosis was refuted: 69 of 101 LongMemEval false refusals had gold evidence in context.
   - It stays a follow-up candidate, not part of this merge.

Shipping nothing was the alternative I considered. I rejected it because the slot-rule patch is opt-in and harmless, carries the rag.py scores/reranker interface that any later answerability work needs, and repairs the harness TypeError. Its marketing value is near zero and the wording below reflects that.
required_adjustments:
Base: the verifier's combined patch, which is the design plus tests/test_abstention_verifier.py (sha256 21a2f7e6a36a607264046b2db4b7cfe254739fd59043db436823f6d7d2e75342). It applies to a fresh snapshot copy with git apply. Every change below is driven by probes or dev data only. Use no held-out data while making them.

Before merge (slot rule v2):
1. Relation names. In _relation_names, apply the _STOP/_CALENDAR exclusion only to capitalised runs that are NOT directly after the relation word. "my brother Will", "my daughter June", "my sister April", "my colleague Jan" and "my partner Jun" must fill the name slot.
2. Head noun. Use the relation_name slot only when the relation word is the head noun ("my sister's name", "what is my brother called"). For possessive modifiers ("my mum's shop", "my brother's dog", "my son's teacher") fall back to the generic new-capitalised-name check. The probe "What's the name of my mum's shop?" with "...called Bloemkast" must be answered.
3. Duration and distance number words. Remove standalone 'a', 'an' and 'half' from the number words in _DURATION and _DISTANCE, keeping phrases like "half an hour" and "an hour". Drop the bare \d+:\d\d clock-time match, so "twice a week" no longer fills "How long is my yoga class?" and "8:30" no longer fills a duration.
4. Money and frequency fillers. Accept a bare number within the anchor window as a money filler ("Rent went up to 1,450 a month"). Add 'biweekly', 'bimonthly' and 'fortnightly' to the frequency words.
5. CLI warning. Print a stderr warning when `ask --abstain` is used with a non-extractive generator, with --no-rerank, or when context['reranker']['status'] != 'applied'. The flag is otherwise a silent no-op. Better still, reject --abstain with --generator gemini.
6. Tests. Turn the verifier's 6 expectedFailure tests into normal passing tests as fixes 1 to 4 land; under pytest, a unittest expectedFailure that passes counts as a failure. Keep the 3 safe-property tests. Add tests for the fix-5 warning. The full suite must pass (it was 184 tests, or 187 plus 6 xfail with the verifier file).
7. Re-check. Re-run the dev replays (calib and bench-dev): acceptance must stay 100% and balanced must not drop. Then run ONE held-out confirmation per set (bench test via `evaluation.ablation --split test --candidate-limit 20 --abstain-threshold 0.0`, and the LongMemEval/LoCoMo replays on the saved contexts) and report it as a "post-adjustment confirmation".
   - If acceptance falls below 95% on bench or 90% on an external, revert the offending fix.
   - Do not tune anything in response to those numbers.
   - Keep the frozen-version table below as the pre-registered result.
8. Housekeeping:
   - Correct the gold_queries.json hash in all docs and notes to a93ca70ff6d40b458db4d82a04fc79b8c7f91dd599840f0e2f96482153d00f25 (…0f25; the design text wrongly wrote …0e07).
   - Leave the library default at abstain_threshold=None and ABSTAIN_THRESHOLD=0.0 (no logit floor).
   - The CLI help must say "experimental".
   - Commit the author's rewritten seeds and gold_queries.json together with the code (`build_dataset --check` passes).
   - Copy the slot-rule-v2/tools and verify-slot-rule-v2/tools scripts into docs/progress/ so the scratch dir is not the only copy.

Not merged (F6-answerability-model), with the conditions for a later round:
- (a) Cache load failure for the process. Never download inside a request; require an explicit one-time fetch command or an allow-download flag, and honour HF_HUB_OFFLINE.
- (b) Remove the '<speaker>: ' prefix from passage_text.
- (c) Make attribution fail closed when the named person is neither a speaker nor mentioned in any source.
- (d) Keep session dates for temporally anchored questions.
- (e) Re-tune on dev only, re-freeze, then do one held-out run. Report bootstrap CIs plus the attribution and paraphrase ablations.
- Even then it can be opt-in only unless external acceptance reaches 90% or more.
report_wording:
Extractive abstention (experimental, off by default). CogniMem's extractive generator has an optional abstention rule ("slot rule v2", enabled with `ask --abstain`). It refuses a question only when the question asks for a specific type of answer (a name, place or organisation, occupation, frequency, amount of money, duration or distance) and no confidently reranked memory contains a filler of that type. It does not detect unanswerable questions in general. Yes/no, who/when/why, opinion, choice, counting and date-arithmetic questions are never refused.

What the numbers show:
- On our benchmark's held-out test split (270 questions, 23 unanswerable) it keeps 99.6% of answerable questions and refuses 17.4% of unanswerable ones. Balanced accuracy is 58.5% against 50.0% with no abstention, better than chance (hypergeometric p=0.0002).
- It never makes things worse: answerable acceptance is 98.4% or higher on every held-out set.

What the numbers do not show:
- It gives no useful gain on external conversational benchmarks. LongMemEval: balanced 52.6%, +2.6 points, from 2 of 30 unanswerables refused; not significant, p=0.096. LoCoMo: 50.0%, +0.0, with refusal precision equal to the unanswerable base rate.
- External unanswerables are mostly false-premise or entity-swap questions. The memory does contain an answer of the right type, just about a different person or event, and a type check cannot catch that.
- The benchmark gain rests on 23 AI-authored unanswerable questions that were not human-validated, written in the "attribute never stated" style the rule targets. One question moves bench-test refusal by about 4 points.
- The rule's patterns are hand-written and English-only.
- The benchmark-test numbers use the rewritten unanswerable set, so they are not comparable with earlier F6 figures (for example the old 86.3%).
- The rule was frozen before any held-out evaluation, and each held-out set was scored once. The post-merge adjustments came only from probes, and the post-adjustment confirmation is reported separately.

A learned answerability model (local QNLI cross-encoder) was also evaluated. It has a stronger signal (benchmark test 74.7% balanced; LoCoMo +6.2 points, 95% CI [+3.8, +8.7]) but rejects about a quarter of external answerable questions: 78.5% acceptance on LongMemEval, 76.1% on LoCoMo. It has known defects and is not shipped. Its LongMemEval gain (+5.9) is not statistically significant (CI [-2.7, +14.7]), and a simple wording-template baseline scores higher there (62.2%), though only by refusing half of all answerable questions. Default answer quality is unchanged: abstention is off unless requested.

Adoption rule (acceptance >= 95 bench / >= 90 externals, AND balanced gain >= +3 on both externals):
- Slot rule v2: acceptance passes; gain is +2.6 / +0.0, so FAIL.
- QNLI model: acceptance 78.5 / 76.1, so FAIL; gain is +5.9 / +6.2 as point estimates.

Abstention precision:
- Slot rule v2: dev-calib 100, bench-dev 100, bench-test 80.0, LongMemEval 22.2 (base rate 6.0), LoCoMo 22.6 (base rate 22.5).
- QNLI model: 93.3, 85.7, 63.2, 9.0, 30.6.

Grounded correctness against no abstention:
- Slot rule v2: bench-test 90.4 vs 89.3, LongMemEval 31.4 vs 31.4, LoCoMo 16.7 vs 16.5.
- QNLI model: 91.5 vs 89.3, 29.8 vs 30.0, 23.7 vs 16.4.

Significance:
- Slot rule v2 against a random abstainer at the same rate: bench-test p=0.0002, LongMemEval p=0.096, LoCoMo p=0.56.
- QNLI model, bootstrap 95% CI of the balanced gain: bench-test [+14.2, +35.5], LoCoMo [+3.8, +8.7], LongMemEval [-2.7, +14.7].

Added latency per ask:
- Slot rule v2: p50 0.007 ms, p95 0.014 ms.
- QNLI model: p50 86 / 128 / 233 ms (bench-test / LoCoMo / LongMemEval).

The post-adjustment confirmation for slot rule v2 is to be appended as a separate row after the merge fixes.
